I will keep the farm simple and stable this year. In Quzhou County, I trust the wheat and summer maize rotation because I know it fits the land, the water situation, and the local weather. At my age, I do not want to spread myself across too many crops that need more sorting, more hand labor, or more market risk. I will put all my land into winter wheat first, then follow it with summer maize on the same fields. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I want steady emergence, better yield, and less risk of losing the stand. I will fertilize enough to support grain production but not chase extreme yield, because input costs matter to me. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical and common for me, and I will irrigate a few key times instead of too often. I will spray only when needed to keep weeds, insects, and disease from taking too much yield. This is the plan I would choose because it is familiar, manageable, and dependable for my conditions.
